_comment: Things a LÖVE game can do on desktop but not in the browser. Used by the editor (compat.js) and package.py. 'scope' is the text a pattern runs on: 'source' (comments removed) or 'code' (comments and string contents removed). A match is skipped if its line matches 'unless', or the file matches 'unlessFile'. 'once' reports only the first match in a project. {1} in a message is the pattern's first group.

rules.message: require('{1}') fails on the web: it's part of LuaJIT, and the browser runs standard Lua 5.1. Wrap it in pcall and fall back to plain Lua.
require('{1}') fails on the web: browsers don't allow raw network sockets. Use require('https') for HTTP requests.
64-bit integer literals need LuaJIT's FFI, so this file won't load on the web.
love.graphics.{1} isn't available on the web: compute shaders need desktop graphics APIs, and browsers only offer WebGL 2 here.
{1} can't run programs in the browser.
The jit global is nil on the web, so jit.{1} raises an error. Guard it with 'if jit then'.
Threads work on the web, but they take turns with the game on one CPU core rather than running in parallel.
